main_text.p: fus, qui ut se vidit in extremo constitutum periculo, necem intentat invasori. Cumque in progressu pejor aggressoris existat conditio, sic ut ex offensore fiat defensor suæ vitæ, & ex voluntario & temerario aggressore, necessarius. Quæsitum, an illi tuto liceat adversarium, quem primum fuerat aggressus, necare, quo mortis periculum evadat? Respondeo, nullo jure poterit, qui sine causa adversarium aggressus est primitus, eundem occidere. Ratio 1. est, quia non præsumitur justam occidendi causam habuisse, qui inspecto initio, non facit aliquid ad defensionem, sed Argum. l.52. §.1. ad offensionem. Verum qui D. Adl. Aquil. primùm aggressus est adversarium principii ratione, justam l.s.11.D.[?] litigandi causam non habuit, si quadr. Paup. l.6. quia iniquus offensor. Ergo Cod. Ad & culpæ reus habebitur. l.Jul. de vi Publica.
Quò etiam facit, quod quan- l. quod

page.notes: The first word "fus," is a fragment carried over from the previous page and is kept as printed. The marginal references are printed in small type and some are hard to read: "l.52. §.1." and "l.s.11.D." may be "l.52." and "l.5.§.11.D." respectively; both are doubtful. "si quadr." is printed with a long-s form and is read as "si". The catchword "do" completes "quando", which is split across the page end; the main text ends at the hyphenated "quan-".
